## Source-support finding

### F1 — Lead weakens the hypothetical qualification in the preparation preference

Draft: “Lind skulle välja att göra försöket igen, men **vill avsätta mer tid för förberedelser**.”

Source: “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but **I would leave an extra week for preparation**.”

The first lead clause preserves “would choose”; the second changes the corresponding “would leave” into present “vill”. The exact separately checkable proposition is that Lind presently wants to allocate more preparation time, whereas the source gives her choice of preparation allowance in a hypothetical repeat trial. The source does not rule out its precise negation. A concrete source-compatible counterexample is that Lind has no present wish or intention to allocate any preparation time because there is no expansion decision, while she would allow an extra week if another trial were chosen. That fully fits S17/S19.

This is a small modal precision issue, not an invented endorsement or an assertion that expansion has already occurred. The rest of the lead supplies substantial conditional context, and the full quotation is accurate. The smallest repair is nevertheless available without changing voice or framing:

“Lind skulle välja att göra försöket igen, men **skulle avsätta mer tid för förberedelser**.”

The source supports that exact hypothetical preference. “Mer tid” is a supported generalization of an extra week; the exact extra week remains in the full quotation.

No other source-support findings. The draft keeps customer agency; attributes the subjective benefit; retains the workload limitation and the note's non-attribution; distinguishes assignment from completion; does not invent savings, satisfaction, recommendation to every housing company, competitor comparisons, physical scenes or emotions; and identifies the actual supplied reading destination.

## Separate translated-quotation check

### Quotation 1

Source: “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

Draft: “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.”

Same meaning, stance, agency and direct, practical voice. “Redan hade gjort” retains the anterior action; “Kategorierna var våra” retains the emphatic division of ownership and help. Swedish speech is idiomatic. No concrete translation obstruction and no repair required.

### Quotation 2

Source: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

Draft: “Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att registrera de första felanmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad kommer i gång.”

Same comparison, personal recommendation and conditional stance. “Felanmälningarna” renders “reports” according to the explicit repair-report context. “Nästa byggnad kommer i gång” preserves the source's building-for-rollout metonym; the supplied trial context makes the intended reading available in Swedish. There is no concrete obstruction warranting a correction merely for a preferred fuller wording. The singular “Jag skulle” does not promise that the team will expand. No translation finding.

### Quotation 3

Source: “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

Draft: “Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen. Att ha en gemensam vy över felanmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser.”

Same conditional positive assessment, team benefit and concrete reservation. “Gemensam vy” is warranted by the shared-log/shared-information context; it does not add a technical capability beyond the supplied one view of reports. “Avsätta en extra vecka” naturally expresses the speaker's extra preparation allowance. The measured findings do not become her reason for endorsing the trial. No translation finding.

## Completion status

Complete: every factual/attributed proposition in the complete draft and all three translated quotations have been checked, with separate pronoun-feature accounting. Unresolved finding: F1, the lead's present “vill” versus source-conditional “would”; proposed minimal repair above. No draft or source files changed.

None. Each independently checkable factual or attributed proposition has support at its actual scope. In particular, the count retains exclusions, median assignment time stays distinct from repair completion, different workloads remain stated, and the note's non-attribution is not converted into knowledge that software had no effect. The customer's own reported benefit and conditional preference are preserved as the customer's assessment. The link is described as a reading document. No universal recommendation, money saving, resident satisfaction, physical scene or emotion is added.

## Translated-quotation findings

Q1 preserves the desired evening/morning information relationship, customer ownership of the categories, and Svale's assisting role. Its first-person collective voice and plain matter-of-fact tone remain. No concrete meaning or voice obstruction found.

Q2 preserves greater time spent reaching agreement than entering the first reports, the first-person conditional recommendation and its before-next-building timing. One local target-language obstruction remains:

**T1 — “innan nästa byggnad kommer i gång”.** In Swedish, “byggnaden kommer i gång” leaves the activity unstated and treats the building itself as something that starts operating. English “before the next building starts” is shorthand for the rollout/activity at the next building. Here the supplied trial and not-yet-expanded context settles that activity. The reader can recover the intended meaning, but the literal subject–predicate pairing is not idiomatic clear speech for a housing building. Smallest supported repair: **“innan försöket startar i nästa byggnad”**. This makes the settled activity explicit while retaining the same future timing and conditional recommendation; it does not assert that expansion has happened or been decided. This is a translation finding, not a missing-source claim.

Q3 preserves the conditional choice to repeat, the unhedged first-person assessment of usefulness, the contrast “men”, and one extra preparation week. “En gemensam vy” is a natural context-specific rendering of “one view”, not an added performance claim. The practical and qualified voice remains. No other concrete translation obstruction found.
